newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks expected to start new China era strong.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks expected to start new China era strong.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are set to welcome a new era under China with firm gains at the opening on Thursday, with China's red chip stocks likely to lead the way.
The market was closed on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday to mark Hong Kong's change in sovereignty at midnight of June 30. Today is the first trading day under Chinese rule.
"So far there have been no major hiccups. I would be looking for the market to generally go better," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
The Hang Seng blue chip index scored an all-time closing high on Friday, rising 68.77 points to 15,196.79.

Brokers said enthusiasm surrounding Hong Kong's change in sovereignty should boost trading in red chips on Thursday, while the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday would lift sentiment.
"Market sentiment remains good. May be we will see the index surge higher at the opening," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.

While some brokers saw property stocks coming under pressure from the new government's plans to increase housing, Osborn said the absence of short-term measures against speculators was encouraging. "The measures were discounted anyway," he added.
